about: Bedrock sound categories of TF's sound events, from the SoundSource that TF's playSound call sites use (Java SoundSource -> Bedrock category: BLOCKS block, HOSTILE hostile, NEUTRAL neutral, PLAYERS player, AMBIENT ambient, WEATHER weather, RECORDS record, MUSIC music). tools/sounds/baseline/generate.ps1 applies, in order: 'events' (exact ids or wildcards), then music.* music, music_disc.* record, block.* block, item.* player (the user of an item is a player: Player.playSound and player.getSoundSource() are PLAYERS), and entity.twilightforest.<mob>.* the mob's own SoundSource, read from TF's entity classes (HOSTILE for subclasses of Monster, Spider, Zombie, AbstractSkeleton, Ghast and Slime, NEUTRAL for every other Mob; 'entities' maps the event names that are not entity ids). Where TF plays an event with several sources, the source of its main call site wins ('why'). block.twilightforest.cicada.why: block/CicadaBlock.java, block/CritterBlock.java, block/entity/CicadaBlockEntity.java, client/MovingCicadaSoundInstance.java: SoundSource.NEUTRAL (only block/CicadaJarBlock.java plays it as BLOCKS)

entity.twilightforest.fortification_shie.why: item/FortificationWandItem.java: Player.playSound (PLAYERS); the Lich plays it too (entity/boss/Lich.java)
entity/boss/Lich.java: Lich.playSound (a Monster: HOSTILE), its only call site
components/entity/FortificationShieldAttachment.java: SoundSource.PLAYERS; the Lich plays it too (entity/boss/Lich.java)

item.twilightforest.transformation_powde.why: util/entities/EntityUtil.java: the transformed mob's getSoundSource() (TF's transformations are mostly animals: NEUTRAL)
